subject: Business Models
title: Homejoy: The Leakage Problem
description: A short lesson to help you apply Homejoy: The Leakage Problem.

hook.text: Homejoy matched cleaners with homeowners. It grew to $35 million in revenue—then collapsed.

buildup.text: Customers loved their cleaners. After the first booking through Homejoy, they hired directly and skipped the platform.

discovery.text: Homejoy had no ongoing value. The match was its only service. Once made, the platform was unnecessary.

twist.text: Handy, a competitor, survived by offering insurance and payment processing—ongoing reasons to stay on-platform.

climax.text: Marketplaces die when their only value is the initial match. Ongoing value prevents disintermediation.

punchline.text: Match once, lose the customer forever. Without ongoing value, you're disposable.

quiz.question: Why did Homejoy fail?
options: Customers hired cleaners directly after the first match
